messages:
maria: Heads up — onboarding hit a weird combo of issues with the embeddings/rerank endpoints in the sample app. Node SDK vs Python SDK returning different vector shapes and our batching helper docs are ambiguous.

maria: Node sample app sends batch of 3, gets back 3 arrays of length 1536. Python sample returns length 768 for the same model env. Not sure if sampleapp or SDK is doing truncation/quantization.

liam: Which model are you hitting? Could be model alias mismatch (e.g., `redwood/embedding-2k` vs `embedding-1k`).

maria: Hitting `embed-kuiper-v1` (from quickstart). Both envs set MODEL=embed-kuiper-v1. Logs attached in thread.

sophie: @maria can you paste the request payloads? If batching helper changes order or pads differently we might be reading dims wrong.

maria: Sure — Node request (abridged):
```json
{
  "model": "embed-kuiper-v1",
  "input": ["a","b","c"],
  "batching": { "max_batch_size": 8 }
}
```
Node response: `[[0.01,0.02,...(1536 floats)], [...], [...]]`

maria: Python request (abridged):
```py
client.embeddings.create(model="embed-kuiper-v1", input=["a","b","c"])
```
Python response looks like: `[[0.003,...(768 floats)], [...], [...]]`

sam: That smells like Python SDK might be calling a fallback model behind the scenes due to an auth/retry quirk. We've seen refresh token race where a 401 triggers a retry against a lower-capacity model.

sophie: Also check the `embedding` field name. We had a change where some SDKs return `embedding` and others `embedding_vector` depending on the parser. If the sample app picks the first field it sees, shape could differ.

maria: Good point — Node response body contains `embedding` array. Python `Embedding` object reports `.vector` length 768 in the sampleapp wrapper.

paul: Can someone repro with `curl` to remove SDK layers?

maria: Repro with curl:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"embed-kuiper-v1","input":["a","b","c"]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```
Result: `1536`. So service returns 1536. That suggests Python SDK parsing or local sampleapp wrapper transforms vector.

liam: That isolates it to the Python client or sampleapp. @sophie any recent changes to the Python EmbeddingResponse class?

sophie: There was a refactor two weeks ago to add lazy quantization support. It added `vector` and `quantized_vector` fields and a backwards-compat shim that maps `embedding` -> `vector` when present. Looks okay but maybe the shim prefers `quantized_vector` if `content_encoding` header is set.

maria: Another wrinkle: when we use the batching helper in the sampleapp, retries sometimes resend batches that overlap — causing duplicate items in the backend and then a post-processing dedupe that drops alternate vectors (leading to shorter arrays in wrapper). So retry + dedupe + field name mismatch = confusing output.

sam: That's the auth/retry behavior I worried about. If token refresh triggers a retry and the helper doesn't attach idempotency keys, server can dedupe by payload hash and return fallbacks. We should add idempotency to batching helper and ensure SDKs pass it through.

paul: Agreed. Quick mitigation: sampleapp should validate that the returned vector length matches model profile in model catalog (we have a JSON mapping). If mismatch, surface a clear error instead of silently subsampling.

sophie: I'll open a mini PR to make the Python wrapper prefer the explicit `embedding` field and assert length == model_dims. Also add a debug env var SAMPLEAPP_STRICT_EMBED_DIMS=true.

liam: I'll add idempotency header support to `batching-helper` and wire it into Node+Python SDKs. Should fix duplicate-send dedupe edge-case.

maria: Thanks. One more UX request: the onboarding quickstart should show a `curl` check early (like you did, paul) so users can confirm server dims before blaming SDKs. Can we patch docs?

dev-bot: deploy noted: patch/doc-update-preview available in #docs/pr-1204 (preview link) :rocket:

maria: Perfect. For tracking: filing a small DX bug to capture three actions — (1) Python shim fix, (2) batching-helper idempotency, (3) quickstart curl check.

sam: If anyone wants to pair on a repro I'm free this afternoon. Happy to help validate after PRs land. :+1:

maria: Thanks all — will drop the bug link here when created.
